Reject a Stopping Rule an Optimizer Cannot Evaluate

Source: R/methods.R
check_criterion.Rd

Compares what the optimizer's criterion reads against what the optimizer can supply, and stops if the rule asks for something absent.

Usage

check_criterion(optimizer)

Arguments

optimizer

An optimizer.

Value

Invisibly TRUE; raises an error otherwise.

Details

Call this at the top of a user-defined minimize method. A rule needing a gradient, handed to a method that computes none, would sit testing NULL at every iteration and never fire; the run would then end on its iteration budget and report a reason nowhere near the truth. Rejecting it here, by name, is what check_optimizer tests for.

What an optimizer can supply is declared by optimizer_provides, whose default claims a gradient. Override that when the method computes none.

See also

optimizer_provides, crit_needs

Examples

check_criterion(bfgs())
try(check_criterion(nelder_mead(criterion = crit_grad())))
#> Error : The stopping rule needs gradient, which nelder-mead does not provide.
#>   Choose a criterion this optimizer can evaluate, or a method that provides it.
